body:
Hi, thank you for your report!

Could you please attach a debug log of the crash?
```sh
WAYLAND_DEBUG=1 path/to/godot --verbose 2>&1 | tee debug.log
```

This will dump all Wayland events (including any input sent to the editor) and print general verbose messages.

It would be very useful to know more about your setup, like the compositor used and whether you use display scaling (e.g. 1.25x or 2x for HiDPI) as it's a common source of trouble. You could also try running the engine with `GODOT_WAYLAND_DISABLE_LIBDECOR` set to `1` and see if it makes a difference.

I found starting full-screen from CLI to be the **only** way to workaround the Editor crashing on startup.

I use `-f` for full-screen then set screen, windowed mode and window geometry:
`godot -e -f -w --screen 0 --position 0,0 --resolution 1920x1080`

## Reproduction
There seems to be some persisted information that toggles state of the problem reproducing.  After using the workaround above, I have sometimes found launching the editor works perfectly fine!?

I managed to get it to start crashing again using:
` -e -w --screen 0 --position 0,0 --resolution 1920x1080 --display-driver wayland --rendering-method forward_plus`

## WAYLAND_DEBUG
Since I started writing, the request re. `WAYLAND_DEBUG=1` was added so I've done that and attached 3 logs:

- [godot-editor-wayland+forward_plus+fullscreen=works.log](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/25525848/godot-editor-wayland%2Bforward_plus%2Bfullscreen.works.log)
- [godot-editor-wayland+forward_plus+windowed+nopos=crash.log](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/25525849/godot-editor-wayland%2Bforward_plus%2Bwindowed%2Bnopos.crash.log)
- [godot-editor-wayland+forward_plus+windowed=crash.log](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/25525850/godot-editor-wayland%2Bforward_plus%2Bwindowed.crash.log)

## Details
- I have `prefer_wayland=true`.
- I'm using `-e` (editor mode) since my editor was otherwise crashing every time!
- Multi-GPU AMD dGPU and iGPU
- Godot Engine v4.6.1.stable.official.14d19694e
- Vulkan 1.4.328 - Forward+ - Using Device #0: AMD - AMD Radeon RX 6800 XT (RADV NAVI21)
- Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS with KDE
- In case relevant for reproduction:
  - I have kisak MESA drivers installed for Quest/Steam use from https://ppa.launchpadcontent.net/kisak/kisak-mesa/ubuntu/  Reported when using the GL renderer:
    `OpenGL API 4.6 (Core Profile) Mesa 24.2.0-devel - Compatibility - Using Device: AMD - AMD Radeon RX 6800 XT (radeonsi, navi21, LLVM 18.1.7, DRM 3.58, 6.8.0-100-generic)`
  - I have AMD ROCM drivers installed (for ollama) from https://repo.radeon.com/amdgpu/6.2.2/ubuntu 
- Previously tried workarounds from other bugs:
  - `GDK_BACKEND=x11` from, I think, a StackOverflow suggestion.  Still crashes but reports 3 extra crashes before!
  - `--rendering-method gl_compatibility --gpu-index 0|1|2` from #116652 
  - Force to X11 on either GPU from https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/95566 :
    - `DRI_PRIME=0 godot -e  --display-driver x11 --gpu-index 0` (force X11 with dGPU = works)
    - `DRI_PRIME=1 godot -e  --display-driver x11 --gpu-index 1` (force X11 with iGPU = works)

See also:
- https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/116148 
- https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/104752

I have attached two crash log files, both with WAYLAND_DEBUG=1 and one also setting GODOT_WAYLAND_DISABLE_LIBDECOR=1.

1. [debug.log](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/25567918/debug.log)
2. [debug_disable_libdecor.log](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/25567919/debug_disable_libdecor.log)

**Details**

- Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS with GNOME Shell 46.0
- No display scaling using two 144hz 1440p monitors.
- Vulkan 1.4.328 using AMD Radeon RX 9070 XT (RADV GFX1201).  The CPU's iGPU is disabled in BIOS.
- Driver version Mesa 25.3.5 - kisak-mesa PPA

Hi, thank you for your report! It looks like you are all crashing due to an invalid resolution being set, specifically one of the two dimensions is set to 0.

#104752 and #116862 fail in the exact same way. Because of this I think I'll consolidate everything into the oldest report as I'm pretty sure that the underlying cause is the same.

Cya there!
